problem.text: The author reports nested static_for_pack failures with VC++ older than 17.13. The change replaces template-lambda launch selection with explicit kernel-pointer tables; the compiler-version boundary is an author claim, not independently verified.

reasoning.text: Explicit tables retain compile-time kernel specializations while moving runtime selection to array indexing. This avoids the nested generic-lambda dispatch implicated by the author, at the cost of manually enumerating supported variants.

impact.text: Paged cache wrappers now explicitly reject bitrates outside 2–8 before indexing. Packing, unpacking, sign packing and reconstruction also gain cudaPeekAtLastError checks.

source_notes.text: A whole-parent-tree literal search found no VC++ occurrences.

The inspected discussions report distinct problems: #7, “quantizing model: undefined symbol: __cxa_call_terminate,” describes a Linux/Conda toolchain mismatch; #15, “`cogito-v1-preview-qwen-32B` generates incoherent output for bpw <= 2.5,” discusses regularization; #12, “Qwen2.5 Coder 0.5B Instruct | ValueError: Unsupported type in stop_conditions,” discusses chat mode selection. None supplies verification of this VC++ workaround.

limitations: No CUDA compilation, GPU execution or performance measurement was performed; compatibility with the stated VC++ versions remains unestablished.
The scalar check validates transcribed selector arithmetic only, not C++ function-pointer launch support or numerical kernel correctness.

chapters.title: Explicit specialization tables for CUDA launches

claims.text: Weight packing, unpacking, tile quantization and reconstruction use eight-entry tables indexed by K−1, covering 1–8 bits per weight. Contiguous cache operations use seven-entry tables indexed by bits−2; paged operations use 7×7 tables with key bitrate as the first dimension and value bitrate as the second.

The selected kernels retain their existing algorithms and launch arguments: cache kernels encode/decode 32-value groups with independent key/value specializations; weight packing operates on 256-value tiles; quantize_tiles retains its scratch-buffer batching; reconstruction retains 256-thread blocks handling eight packed tiles. This is dispatch restructuring, not a new compression format.
A bounded Python transcription verified that all eight weight selectors and all 49 key/value combinations recover the original specialization parameters.
static_for_pack remains defined. util.h adds a commented table example and the compiler warning rather than removing the helper.

findings.description: Direct table indexing introduces an unchecked out-of-range access in pack_trellis and unpack_trellis for unsupported K.
findings.trigger: Call either native wrapper with K=9 and tensors satisfying its shape checks, including packed final dimension 144 and unpacked final dimension 256.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject unsupported bitrate without accessing outside the specialization table.
findings.actual_behavior: The new expression indexes element 8 of an eight-entry table. Existing shape checks do not reject this construction; the previous dispatch simply selected no kernel.

verification.description: Whole-parent-tree search finds both native bindings and a Python pack_trellis helper that forwards quant_args['K'] without a local range check. The unpack call in that helper is commented out. Reach is established for direct extension callers and this packing helper, not for every conversion workflow.
verification.limits: No claim that normal conversion settings produce K=9.

verification.description: Computed packed dimension 144 and table index 8 for K=9.
verification.limits: Arithmetic only; no native out-of-bounds access or GPU launch was executed.

annotation.summary: Replaces template-lambda CUDA dispatch with explicit specialization tables to address reported older-VC++ failures, adds launch-error checks, and leaves unsupported weight bitrates vulnerable to unchecked indexing.

argv: w=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]; c=[2,3,4,5,6,7,8]; pairs=[[(k,v) for v in c] for k in c]; assert all(w[k-1]==k for k in w); assert all(pairs[k-2][v-2]==(k,v) for k in c for v in c); print('8 weight selectors and 49 cache pairs match original template parameters'); print('K=9: packed last dimension=',256*9//16,'; index=',9-1,'; table length=',len(w))
